# Rise and Battle the Day

## Scripture
"Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong." – 1 Corinthians 16:13

## Reflection
The alarm goes off, and the battle begins. Before your feet hit the floor, the enemy is already at work—whispering that you can hit snooze, that today doesn't matter, that you can coast. But Paul's charge to the church at Corinth wasn't a suggestion; it was a command. Watch. Stand firm. Act like men. Be strong.

Notice the order. Watchfulness comes first. A soldier who sleeps through his watch leaves the whole camp exposed. The same is true for us. If we drift through our mornings without prayer, without Scripture, without intention, we hand the enemy ground before breakfast. Strength isn't born in the moment of crisis—it's built in the quiet disciplines of the ordinary day.

But here's the good news: this strength isn't self-manufactured. It flows from a God who never sleeps, never tires, and never abandons His post. Your job isn't to conjure power. It's to show up, stay alert, and stand on the Rock. Courage isn't the absence of fear—it's obedience in the presence of it. So rise. The day is yours to take ground for the Kingdom.

## Daily Challenge
Do 25 pushups, and with each rep, thank God that He is your strength and your shield. Then spend five minutes in prayer before you touch your phone.
